FEDERALREGISTER

Washington, Wednesday, March 24, 1948
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT  
PROCLAMATION 2772  
P an  A m erican W e ek, 1948 
BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES  
OF AM ERICA 
A  PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS the people of the United  
States of America and the people of the  
other republics of the Americas, inspired  
by sentiments of Pan-Americanism and  
devoted to the policy of the Good Neigh­
bor, are united by bonds of friendship  
and mutual respect, which have grown  
strong through inter-American coopera­
tion in many fields of human activity;  
and
WHEREAS the concept of a Western  
Hemisphere community of nations is  
expressed through the principles, agen­
cies, and procedures of the Inter-Amer­
ican System i "  the foundations of which  
were laid at the First International Con­
ference of American States in the year  
1890; and
WHEREAS the Ninth International  
Conference of American States is soon  
to be held at Bogotá, Colombia, to con­
solidate and strengthen the Inter-Amer­
ican System, in order that the common 
will of thè American republics may be 
more perfectly realized, in consonance  
with the principles and purposes of the  
United Nations; and
WHEREAS the Governing Board of  
the Pan American Union has resolved  
that April 14, the founding date of the  
Union, should be officially observed each  
year by every member country as Pan  
American Day, a custom which the  
United States has followed:
NOW, THEREFORE, I, HARRY S.  
TRUMAN, President of the United States  
of America, do hereby proclaim Wednes­
day, April 14, 1948, as Pan American  
Day, and in order to broaden the scope  
of the observance of this anniversary, I  
designate the week beginning April 11,  
1948, as Pan American Week. I call upon  
the officials of the Government to display  
the flag of the United States on all pub­
lic buildings during that week; and I  
invite the people of the several States,  
Territories, and possessions of the United  
States and- the appropriate officials  
thereof, as well as the chinches, schools,  
clubs, and other organizations of our
country, to participate in the observance  
of Pan American Week with suitable  
commemorative displays, exhibits, and  
ceremonies.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have here­
unto set my hand and caused the Seal  
of the United States of America to be  
affixed.'
DONE at the City of Washington this  
20th day of March in the year of our  
Lord nineteen hundred and  
[ se a l] forty-eight, and of the Inde­
pendence of the United States  
of America the one hundred and sev­
enty-second.
H arry  S. T rum an
By the President:
W illard  L. T h o rp,
Acting Secretary of State.

enty-second.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 9938 (13 FR 1555 (Federal Register of March 24, 1948)) revokes Executive Order No. 9544 of April 25, 1945, which had authorized and directed the Secretary of War to assume full control of a public airport in Oregon on described lands (T. 15 S., R. 13 E., Willamette Meridian, 1,520 acres). The held Federal Register text prints the heading of Executive Order 9938 and its paragraphs up to the words “it is intended that the lease shall again be operative and”, where the page breaks (the page notes that the order continues on a later page); the closing words and the signing line are not in the held Federal Register bytes. The American Presidency Project mirror text for the same order is complete and ends with the signing line of March 22, 1948; it is not cited as a source in this claim, because an official copy is held, but it agrees with the Federal Register text up to the break and gives the signing date as March 22, 1948, the date in the register. The operative command is the revocation of Executive Order No. 9544, which the order says “is hereby revoked”. The order also says the lands are included in a twenty-year lease to the City of Redmond that began March 12, 1942, and states the intention that the lease again be operative. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: the order states no effective date in the held bytes, so it took effect when it was signed on March 22, 1948, and the revocation was exhausted by performance on that date. The machine own-term candidate of 1962-03-12 is the end of the Redmond lease described in the order; it is a fact about the lease and not an end of the order's revocation, so it is not used. A search of the held texts for the order's number found no later order citing it. The Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9544 stays revoked and the lease operates again; that consequence is not a command left to end.

The held Federal Register text breaks off before any words about the effective moment; the mirror text, which is not cited, ties the lease's reactivation to the signing of the order. The date recorded is therefore the signing date, March 22, 1948, with the gap in the held Federal Register bytes disclosed.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The statement about the lease records an intent about an existing lease between other parties; it creates no continuing duty of the order.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 9544 stays revoked) survives. The held text has no saving clause and the bounded searches found no later order restoring the revoked control.","scope_check":"One operative clause: the revocation of Executive Order No. 9544 as to the described Oregon airport lands, with the recital of the Redmond lease and the statement of intent. The dossier clause ran across the whole Federal Register page, including its contents list and codification guide; the inventory is corrected to the order text printed in the held bytes, which ends at the page break."}

WHEREAS the people of the United

States and- the appropriate officials

clubs, and other organizations of our
country, to participate in the observance  
of Pan American Week with suitable

ceremonies.

unto set my hand and caused the Seal  
of the United States of America to be  
affixed.'

enty-second.

A  PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS the people of the United  
States of America and the people of the  
other republics of the Americas, inspired  
by sentiments of Pan-Americanism and  
devoted to the policy of the Good Neigh­
bor, are united by bonds of friendship  
and mutual respect, which have grown  
strong through inter-American coopera­
tion in many fields of human activity;  
and
WHEREAS the concept of a Western  
Hemisphere community of nations is  
expressed through the principles, agen­
cies, and procedures of the Inter-Amer­
ican System i "  the foundations of which  
were laid at the First International Con­
ference of American States in the year  
1890; and
WHEREAS the Ninth International  
Conference of American States is soon  
to be held at Bogotá, Colombia, to con­
solidate and strengthen the Inter-Amer­
ican System, in order that the common 
will of thè American republics may be 
more perfectly realized, in consonance  
with the principles and purposes of the  
United Nations; and
WHEREAS the Governing Board of  
the Pan American Union has resolved  
that April 14, the founding date of the  
Union, should be officially observed each  
year by every member country as Pan  
American Day, a custom which the  
United States has followed:
NOW, THEREFORE, I, HARRY S.  
TRUMAN, President of the United States  
of America, do hereby proclaim Wednes­
day, April 14, 1948, as Pan American  
Day, and in order to broaden the scope  
of the observance of this anniversary, I  
designate the week beginning April 11,  
1948, as Pan American Week. I call upon  
the officials of the Government to display  
the flag of the United States on all pub­
lic buildings during that week; and I  
invite the people of the several States,  
Territories, and possessions of the United  
States and- the appropriate officials  
thereof, as well as the chinches, schools,  
clubs, and other organizations of our
country, to participate in the observance  
of Pan American Week with suitable  
commemorative displays, exhibits, and  
ceremonies.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have here­
unto set my hand and caused the Seal  
of the United States of America to be  
affixed.'
DONE at the City of Washington this  
20th day of March in the year of our  
Lord nineteen hundred and  
[ se a l] forty-eight, and of the Inde­
pendence of the United States  
of America the one hundred and sev­
enty-second.

EDERAL REGISTE
VOLUME 13 NUMBER 80
Washington, Friday, April 23, 1948
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9950
Revoking E xecutive O rder N o. 9877 
of J uly 26, 1947, Prescribing the 
Functions of the A rmed F orces
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States, and as President of the 
United States and Commander in Chief 
of the Armed Forces of the United States, 
it is ordered that Executive Order No. 
9877 of July 26, 1947, prescribing the as­
signment^)! primary functions and re­
sponsibilities to the three armed services,

risdiction of the T erritory of H awaii
WHEREAS by Executive Order No. 905, 
dated November 1,1940, of the Governor 
of the Territory of Hawaii, certain here­
inafter-described land in Honolulu, Ter­
ritory of Hawaii, was reserved for the use 
of the United States for military pur­
poses; and
WHEREAS such land is no loiiger 
needed by th^ United States for military 
purposes, and it is deemed advisable and 
in the public interest that it be restored 
to the use of the Territory O f Hawaii: 
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 91 of 
the act of April 30, 1900, 31 Stat. 159, as 
amended by section 7 of the act of May 
27, 1910, 36 Stat.. 447, it is ordered that 
the following-described parcel of land, 
together with all improvements located 
thereon, comprising a portion of the Gov­
ernment Land of Kuwili situate on the 
south side of Prison Road opposite Sum­
ner Street at Kuwili, Iwilei, Honolulu, 
Oahu, Territory of Hawaii, be, and it is 
hereby, restored to the jurisdiction of the 
Territory of Hawaii:
Beginning at the west corner of this par­
cel of land and on the south side of Prison  
Road, the coordinates of said point of begin­
ning referred to Government Survey tri­
angulation station “Kawa” being 163.20 feet  
south and 305.44 feet west, as shown on  
Government Survey Registered Map 2669, and  
running by azimuths measured clockwise  
from true south :

of Prison Road;

July 23, 1930);

Oahu Railway and Land Company;
4. 152°10' 109.70 feet along L. C. Award  
81 F. L. to Kahawaiolaa to the point of be­
ginning.
The area of this parcel is 5,755 square feet,  
more or less.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 9950 (13 FR 2191 (Federal Register of April 23, 1948)) was signed April 21, 1948. The filing stamp printed after the order reads April 21, 1948. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence ordering that Executive Order No. 9877 of July 26, 1947 “be, and it is hereby, revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on April 21, 1948. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. The only other held text containing this order's number is the Federal Register page of April 23, 1948 that reproduces this same order together with Executive Order 9951 (EO_9951.txt); it is the same instrument, not a later one. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9877 of July 26, 1947, which prescribed the functions of the armed forces remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.

VOLUME 13 NUMBER 80
Washington, Friday, April 23, 1948
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9950
Revoking E xecutive O rder N o. 9877 
of J uly 26, 1947, Prescribing the 
Functions of the A rmed F orces
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States, and as President of the 
United States and Commander in Chief 
of the Armed Forces of the United States, 
it is ordered that Executive Order No. 
9877 of July 26, 1947, prescribing the as­
signment^)! primary functions and re­
sponsibilities to the three armed services, 
be, and it is hereby, revoked.
Harry S. T ruman
The White H ouse,
April 21, 1948.
[F. R. Doc. 48-3673; Filed, Apr. 21, 1948;  
4:14 p. m.]
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9951
Restoring C ertain L and of the K uwili  
Park Military R eservation to the J u ­
risdiction of the T erritory of H awaii
WHEREAS by Executive Order No. 905, 
dated November 1,1940, of the Governor 
of the Territory of Hawaii, certain here­
inafter-described land in Honolulu, Ter­
ritory of Hawaii, was reserved for the use 
of the United States for military pur­
poses; and
WHEREAS such land is no loiiger 
needed by th^ United States for military 
purposes, and it is deemed advisable and 
in the public interest that it be restored 
to the use of the Territory O f Hawaii: 
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 91 of 
the act of April 30, 1900, 31 Stat. 159, as 
amended by section 7 of the act of May 
27, 1910, 36 Stat.. 447, it is ordered that 
the following-described parcel of land, 
together with all improvements located 
thereon, comprising a portion of the Gov­
ernment Land of Kuwili situate on the 
south side of Prison Road opposite Sum­
ner Street at Kuwili, Iwilei, Honolulu, 
Oahu, Territory of Hawaii, be, and it is 
hereby, restored to the jurisdiction of the 
Territory of Hawaii:
Beginning at the west corner of this par­
cel of land and on the south side of Prison  
Road, the coordinates of said point of begin­
ning referred to Government Survey tri­
angulation station “Kawa” being 163.20 feet  
south and 305.44 feet west, as shown on  
Government Survey Registered Map 2669, and  
running by azimuths measured clockwise  
from true south :
1. 241 °53' 55.00 feet along the south side  
of Prison Road;
2. 331°53' 98.57 feet along Kuwili Park and  
Playground (Executive Order No. 422 of  
July 23, 1930);
3. 50°33' 56.65 feet along Grant 8564 to  
Oahu Railway and Land Company;
4. 152°10' 109.70 feet along L. C. Award  
81 F. L. to Kahawaiolaa to the point of be­
ginning.
The area of this parcel is 5,755 square feet,  
more or less.
Harry S. T ruman
The W hite H ouse,
April 21, 1948.
[F. R. Doc. 48-3674; Filed, Apr. 21, 1948;
4:14 p. m.]
TITLE 6— AGRICULTURAL CREDIT
Chapter II— Production and Market­
ing Administration (Commodity  
Credit)
Part 245—Irish P otatoes
SUBPART— 1 9 4 8  PRICE SUPPORT PROGRAM
The United States Department of 
Agriculture will support the price of the 
1948 crop of Irish Potatoes at 90 percent 
of parity as of the beginning of the mar­
keting seasons through December 31, 
1948. Such price support will be accom­
plished by means of purchase and loan 
operations, of diversion operations to 
other than normal channels of trade in­
cluding livestock feed and industrial out­
lets, and of export operations. In most 
States purchase operations will termi­
nate generally in the early fall of 1948, 
the exact date possibly varying by States. 
With termination of purchase opera­
tions, price support will be effected by 
loans. Loans must be completed by De­
cember 31, 1948. Final dates for sub­
mission of applications for loans will be 
established by State PMA Committees. 
Loans will bear interest at the rate of 8 
percent per annum and will mature

to band, whichever is earlier. In closing  
the accounts of a man discharged or re­
leased from active duty within the  
ninety-day period, credit shall be made  
only of an amount equal to the value of  
the clothing actually drawn, but in no  
case to exceed the total allowance pay­
able. ,
2. For the purposes of this order, an  
enlistment in any of the services men­
tioned in Section A subsequent to dis­
charge from any other of such services  
shall be considered a reenlistment. An  
allowance under subsection Al shall not  
be payable upon reenlistment within  
three months from date of last discharge,  
or upon recall to active duty within three  
months of last release therefrom, except  
as specified in subsections 5, 6 and 7 of  
this section. A man reenlisted or re­
called to active duty within three months  
of last discharge or release from active  
duty, who bn date of such discharge or  
release was checked undrawn clothing  
allowance in accordance with subsection  
P of this section, shall be entitled to  
credit for such undrawn clothing allow­
ance.
3. The allowance under subsection A2  
shall not be payable to—
(a) Enlisted men advanced in rating  
to chief petty officer while holding a tem­
porary appointment to warrant or com­
missioned rank.
(b> Cooks or stewards on advance­
ment to chief Gook or steward.
(c) Members of Navy, Naval Academy,  
or Coast Guard Academy Bands (band  
members) upon advancement in rating  
to chief petty officer.
4. An enlisted man reduced in rating  
from chief petty officer, cook, or steward  
shall not be required to refund payment  
previously made in accordance with sub­
section A2; and shall not be entitled to  
a second payment on subsequent ad-j  
vancement, or to a payment of quarterly  
maintenance allowance prior to the date  
specified in subsection Cl (a) hereof.
5. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A6 and A9 (b)  
hereof, upon subsequent transfer to,, or  
reenlistment within three months of last  
discharge in, another status which, in  
the case of first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a  
cash clothing allowance as prescribed in  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled to  
a credit of such cash clothing allowance  
without regard to issues in kind in the  
prior status, except that an enlisted man  
entitled to a clothing allowance under  
subsection A9 (b) on first reporting for  
active duty shall not be so entitled.
6. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A7 hereof,  
upon subsequent transfer to, or reenlist­
ment within three months of last dis­
charge in, another status which, in the  
case of a first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a
cash clothing allowance as prescribedjn  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled  
to a credit of such cash clothing allow­
ance without regard to issues in kind in  
the prior status..
7. Enlisted personnel described in sub­
section A9 (a), upon discharge from the  
Naval Reserve'(inactive) for the pur­
pose of enlisting in the Regular Navy or  
Coast Guard within three months from  
date of 'such discharge, shall, if reen­
listed in any of the applicable ratings,  
be entitled to a further cash allowance  
equal to the difference between the cash  
allowance payable under subsection Al  
(a) hereof, and the amount payable un­
der subsection A9 (a), and such enlisted  
personnel shall, if enlisted in other rat­
ings in the Regular Navy or Coast Guard, 
within three months from date of such  
discharge, be entitled to the cash allow­
ances prescribed in subsection Al (b)  
hereof.
Section C. Quarterly Maintenance Al­
lowance.
1. The quarterly maintenance allow­
ance prescribed in section A hereof shall  
be payable on the first day of each quar­
ter to:
(a) Enlisted men entitled to a cloth­
ing allowance under subsections 1, 2, 3,  
4, 5, or 10 of section A, or subsections B5  
and B7 hereof, or who were entitled to a  
clothing allowance under Executive Or­
der 9356 of June 24, 1943, as amended,  
commencing with the first day of the  
quarter following the first anniversary  
of the date on which they were last en­
titled to such clothing allowance.
(b) Enlisted men of the Navy and  
Coast Guard reenlisting within three  
months from date of last discharge, en­
listed men of the Reserve components  
transferred to the regular Service, and  
enlisted men of the Regular and Reserve  
components on active duty transferred  
to the Reserve or to the Retired List and  
retained on active duty or recalled to ac­
tive duty within three months of release  
therefrom, at the rate applicable prior  
to such discharge, transfer, retirement,  
or release, until entitled to a further  
clothing allowance.
2. Enlisted men of the Naval Reserve  
undergoing training leading to a com­
mission, enlisted men of the Naval Re­
serve (inactive) and enlisted men hold­

ances. Enlisted men entitled to a

wise due them on that date.

conducting a program of safety educa­

accidents and reduce the hazards of boat  
operations; and*
WHEREAS the services of the Coast  
Guard are invaluable to the people of  
this Nation, and the work of its per­
sonnel is a vital contribution to the  
strength and stability of our commerce  
and our military reserve power:
NOW, THEREFORE, I, HARRY S.  
TRUMAN, President of the United  
States of America, do hereby proclaim  
August 4 as Coast Guard Day, in recog­
nition of the work of this agency of the  
Government, to the end that its 158th  
and subsequent anniversaries may be  
observed with appropriate ceremonies.  
I request that the flag of the Nation and  
other official flags be displayed on Coast  
Guard Day and that suitable celebra­
tions be conducted to honor the Coast  
Guard and to assist its work by bringing  
public recognition to its program of  
safety at sea.

unto set my hand and caused the Seal

affixed.

Section B. Clothing Allowance.
1. The amount of the cash clothing  
allowances prescribed in subsection Al  
(b) hereof shall be payable on date of  
first enlistment or first reporting for ac­
tive duty, and on date of reenlistment  
or recall to active duty subsequent to  
expiration of three months from date of  
last discharge or release from active duty,  
but shall not actually be paid prior to the
expiration of ninety days from and in­
cluding such date, or date of completion  
of recruit training, or date of advance­
ment to chief petty officer or assignment  
to band, whichever is earlier. In closing  
the accounts of a man discharged or re­
leased from active duty within the  
ninety-day period, credit shall be made  
only of an amount equal to the value of  
the clothing actually drawn, but in no  
case to exceed the total allowance pay­
able. ,
2. For the purposes of this order, an  
enlistment in any of the services men­
tioned in Section A subsequent to dis­
charge from any other of such services  
shall be considered a reenlistment. An  
allowance under subsection Al shall not  
be payable upon reenlistment within  
three months from date of last discharge,  
or upon recall to active duty within three  
months of last release therefrom, except  
as specified in subsections 5, 6 and 7 of  
this section. A man reenlisted or re­
called to active duty within three months  
of last discharge or release from active  
duty, who bn date of such discharge or  
release was checked undrawn clothing  
allowance in accordance with subsection  
P of this section, shall be entitled to  
credit for such undrawn clothing allow­
ance.
3. The allowance under subsection A2  
shall not be payable to—
(a) Enlisted men advanced in rating  
to chief petty officer while holding a tem­
porary appointment to warrant or com­
missioned rank.
(b> Cooks or stewards on advance­
ment to chief Gook or steward.
(c) Members of Navy, Naval Academy,  
or Coast Guard Academy Bands (band  
members) upon advancement in rating  
to chief petty officer.
4. An enlisted man reduced in rating  
from chief petty officer, cook, or steward  
shall not be required to refund payment  
previously made in accordance with sub­
section A2; and shall not be entitled to  
a second payment on subsequent ad-j  
vancement, or to a payment of quarterly  
maintenance allowance prior to the date  
specified in subsection Cl (a) hereof.
5. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A6 and A9 (b)  
hereof, upon subsequent transfer to,, or  
reenlistment within three months of last  
discharge in, another status which, in  
the case of first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a  
cash clothing allowance as prescribed in  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled to  
a credit of such cash clothing allowance  
without regard to issues in kind in the  
prior status, except that an enlisted man  
entitled to a clothing allowance under  
subsection A9 (b) on first reporting for  
active duty shall not be so entitled.

ings in the Regular Navy or Coast Guard,

ances prescribed in subsection Al (b)  
hereof.

lowance.
1. The quarterly maintenance allow­
ance prescribed in section A hereof shall  
be payable on the first day of each quar­
ter to:
(a) Enlisted men entitled to a cloth­
ing allowance under subsections 1, 2, 3,  
4, 5, or 10 of section A, or subsections B5  
and B7 hereof, or who were entitled to a  
clothing allowance under Executive Or­
der 9356 of June 24, 1943, as amended,  
commencing with the first day of the  
quarter following the first anniversary  
of the date on which they were last en­
titled to such clothing allowance.

Coast Guard reenlisting within three  
months from date of last discharge, en­

transferred to the regular Service, and

components on active duty transferred  
to the Reserve or to the Retired List and  
retained on active duty or recalled to ac­

therefrom, at the rate applicable prior  
to such discharge, transfer, retirement,  
or release, until entitled to a further  
clothing allowance.

undergoing training leading to a com­
mission, enlisted men of the Naval Re­

titled to quarterly maintenance allow­
ances. Enlisted men entitled to a

wise due them on that date.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section B governs when the cash clothing allowances are payable, including for reenlisted, recalled and transferred men. It continues until the closing paragraph's sunset on June 30, 1949. Executive Order 10023, signed December 20, 1948 and effective as of December 1, 1948, adds a new subsection 8 to Section B (who is paid the Navy Band allowance, that it is paid once in a period of continuous active duty, and on whose order) for members of the United States Navy Band; under the owner ruling on amendments this is a later event and the clause continues, amended, until the order ends.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The closing paragraph supersedes Executive Orders No. 9744B, No. 9785 and No. 9869, makes the order effective as of July 1, 1948 and provides that it shall “continue in effect for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949”. The supersession was performed on the effective date, July 1, 1948, and the effective-date statement was spent then; the duration command ends on June 30, 1949, so the clause as a whole ends on that date (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins). The end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 9984 (13 FR 4437 (Federal Register of August 3, 1948)) was signed July 31, 1948. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. It prescribes regulations on clothing in kind or cash allowances in lieu of clothing for enlisted personnel of the Navy, Coast Guard, Naval Reserve and Coast Guard Reserve: Section A lists the allowances, Section B governs when the cash allowances are paid, Section C governs the quarterly maintenance allowance, and the closing paragraph supersedes Executive Order No. 9744B, No. 9785 and No. 9869, makes the order effective as of July 1, 1948 and provides that it shall “continue in effect for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949”. On 2026-10-14 every clause is terminated by that own-terms sunset, June 30, 1949. The dossier's forty clause fragments come from the OCR of the allowance tables and are replaced by five operative pieces: the lead, Sections A, B and C, and the closing paragraph. The searches for an earlier end found one later event, Executive Order 10023 (signed December 20, 1948, effective as of December 1, 1948), which adds subsection 11 to Section A and subsection 8 to Section B for members of the Navy Band; it is an amendment and not an end. A held-text search for citations of this order, with and without a trailing footnote digit, found only Executive Order 10023 and its copies and the Federal Register page of August 3, 1948. The Federal Register disposition-note search lists the one hit (Executive Order 10023); the U.S. Code and eCFR searches report no hit.

The end date recorded is June 30, 1949 on the inclusive reading, because the order continues for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949; the exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is disclosed as the alternative.","independent_command_check":"No piece has an independent duration. Sections A to C operate together under the closing paragraph's single fiscal-year sunset.","savings_check":"The order's text has no saving clause. Allowances paid or accrued for enlisted service before the sunset are payments under the regulation; the held text creates no continuing duty after June 30, 1949, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring it.","scope_check":"Five operative pieces replace the dossier's forty fragments: the lead that prescribes the regulations; Section A (entitlements to clothing or cash allowances); Section B (when the cash allowances are payable, including conditions for reenlisted and transferred men); Section C (quarterly maintenance allowance); and the closing paragraph (supersession of three earlier orders, effective date, and duration). The closing paragraph's supersession of Executive Orders No. 9744B, No. 9785 and No. 9869 was performed when the order took effect on July 1, 1948 and is disclosed as exhausted then, but the paragraph also carries the duration, so the clause as a whole ends with the sunset."}

months of last release therefrom, except

components on active duty transferred

retained on active duty or recalled to ac­

listed in any of the applicable ratings,  
be entitled to a further cash allowance  
equal to the difference between the cash  
allowance payable under subsection Al  
(a) hereof, and the amount payable un­
der subsection A9 (a), and such enlisted  
personnel shall, if enlisted in other rat­
ings in the Regular Navy or Coast Guard, 
within three months from date of such  
discharge, be entitled to the cash allow­
ances prescribed in subsection Al (b)  
hereof.
Section C. Quarterly Maintenance Al­
lowance.
1. The quarterly maintenance allow­
ance prescribed in section A hereof shall  
be payable on the first day of each quar­
ter to:
(a) Enlisted men entitled to a cloth­
ing allowance under subsections 1, 2, 3,  
4, 5, or 10 of section A, or subsections B5  
and B7 hereof, or who were entitled to a  
clothing allowance under Executive Or­
der 9356 of June 24, 1943, as amended,  
commencing with the first day of the  
quarter following the first anniversary  
of the date on which they were last en­
titled to such clothing allowance.
(b) Enlisted men of the Navy and  
Coast Guard reenlisting within three  
months from date of last discharge, en­
listed men of the Reserve components  
transferred to the regular Service, and  
enlisted men of the Regular and Reserve  
components on active duty transferred  
to the Reserve or to the Retired List and  
retained on active duty or recalled to ac­
tive duty within three months of release  
therefrom, at the rate applicable prior  
to such discharge, transfer, retirement,  
or release, until entitled to a further  
clothing allowance.

undergoing training leading to a com­
mission, enlisted men of the Naval Re­
serve (inactive) and enlisted men hold­
ing temporary appointments to warrant  
or Commissioned rank shall not be en­
titled to quarterly maintenance allow­
ances. Enlisted men entitled to a  
clothing allowance on the first day of

quarterly maintenance allowance other­
wise due them on that date.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole paragraph closes the offices “shall be closed one-half day on Friday, December 24, 1948” and excuses employees “shall be excused from duty for one-half day on December 24,1948”. Both commands are limited to December 24, 1948, so the clause ended on that day by its own terms. The date is recorded inclusive (the order runs through the end of December 24, 1948); the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10019 (13 FR 7395 (Federal Register of December 4, 1948)) was signed December 2, 1948. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. Its only paragraph orders that the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies in the District of Columbia metropolitan area “shall be closed one-half day on Friday, December 24, 1948”, and that employees in the metropolitan area and in the field service, except those excluded by agency heads for special public reasons or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law, “shall be excused from duty for one-half day on December 24,1948”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated by its own terms: it applies to the single named day, December 24, 1948, and has no operation after that day. The order contains no other command, no condition and no continuing duty. A search of the held texts for the order's number found only the order's own Federal Register page. The Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order.

The end date recorded is December 24, 1948 on the inclusive reading, under which the order runs through the end of that day; the exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is disclosed as the alternative.","independent_command_check":"The closing and the excusal are independent in wording but share the same single day, so both end on the same date. The order creates no continuing duty.","savings_check":"Nothing survives the day: the order excused employees from duty for a half day, grants no continuing leave or pay right beyond that half day, and has no saving clause. The bounded searches found no later instrument that continues or restores it.","scope_check":"The order has one operative paragraph containing two related commands, the closing of offices for one-half day and the excusing of employees for the same half day, both tied to December 24, 1948. The inventory has no other clause."}

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10061 (14 FR 2915 (Federal Register of June 3, 1949)) was signed June 2, 1949. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. It amends Executive Order No. 9871 of July 8, 1947 (as already amended by Executive Order No. 9976 of July 12, 1948) on allowances to enlisted men: item 1 restates Part D of the said order (a daily allowance for men traveling on duty, with meal rates), and item 2 makes the order effective June 1, 1949 and provides that the amended Executive Order No. 9871 and this order “shall continue in effect during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1950, unless sooner modified or revoked”. On 2026-10-14 every clause is terminated by that own-terms sunset, the end of the fiscal year ending June 30, 1950. The wording “unless sooner modified or revoked” requires a search for an earlier modification or revocation. The held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 9871, run with and without a trailing footnote digit, found only Executive Order No. 9976 (the earlier amendment), the Federal Register page that also holds Executive Order 10060, Executive Order 10061 itself and the American Presidency Project copies; no later order modifies or revokes Executive Order No. 9871 or this order. The Federal Register disposition-note search lists one hit for this order, which is a cross-reference attached to Executive Order No. 9976 that points to this order, not a later event. The U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. The dossier splits the order into five fragments (two of them mere continuations of the meal-rate table); the inventory is corrected to the three operative pieces: the amending lead, the restated Part D, and the effective-date and duration item.

The command was exhausted by performance on that date and the end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10068 (14 FR 3883 (Federal Register of July 14, 1949)) was signed July 13, 1949. The filing stamp printed after the order reads July 13, 1949. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence providing that Executive Order No. 2458 of September 20, 1916 “is hereby revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on July 13, 1949. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation, so there is no later recital, amendment or restoration of it in the held corpus. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 2458 of September 20, 1916, which established the Inter-Departmental Board on International Service of Ice Observation, Ice Patrol, and Ocean Derelict Destruction remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists, because the only command in the order is the revocation itself and it was performed when the order took effect on July 13, 1949. The order states no effective date other than signing. The filing stamp printed after the order reads July 13, 1949. If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. No later instrument is claimed as an end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The order creates no independent continuing duty, board, fund or authority that could outlast it; whatever the revoked instrument itself provided is outside this order and is not claimed here.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 2458 of September 20, 1916, which established the Inter-Departmental Board on International Service of Ice Observation, Ice Patrol, and Ocean Derelict Destruction stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole operative sentence says “I hereby revoke the said Executive Orders” Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823 so far as they pertain, respectively, to the three named organizations. The order states no effective date, so the partial revocation took effect when signed on October 10, 1949; the filing stamp reads October 11, 1949, disclosed as the alternative if effectiveness is tied to filing. The command was exhausted by performance and the end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10083 (14 FR 6161 (Federal Register of October 12, 1949)) was signed October 10, 1949. The filing stamp printed after the order reads October 11, 1949, one day after signing. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence beginning “NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 1 of the said International Organizations Immunities Act, I hereby revoke the said Executive Orders” and revoking those three orders only so far as they pertain to the three named organizations. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on October 10, 1949. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Orders Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823, but only so far as they designated the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration, the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees as public international organizations remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists, because the only command in the order is the revocation itself and it was performed when the order took effect on October 10, 1949. The order states no effective date other than signing. The filing stamp printed after the order reads October 11, 1949, one day after signing. If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. No later instrument is claimed as an end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The order creates no independent continuing duty, board, fund or authority that could outlast it; whatever the revoked instrument itself provided is outside this order and is not claimed here.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Orders Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823, but only so far as they designated the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration, the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees as public international organizations stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked. Executive Orders 9698, 9751 and 9823 remain in force as to the other organizations they designate; they are independent instruments and are not claimed here.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence. The order revokes the three earlier orders only as to the three named organizations (its recitals say those organizations have ceased to exist or are in process of liquidation), so the earlier orders continue as to every other organization they designate; that continuation belongs to those earlier orders, not to this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Orders Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823, but only so far as they designated the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration, the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees as public international organizations stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked. Executive Orders 9698, 9751 and 9823 remain in force as to the other organizations they designate; they are independent instruments and are not claimed here.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole paragraph adopts existing regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Career Compensation Act of 1949 and ends with the sentence “This order shall take effect on October 1, 1949, and shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950”. Five later orders, 10098, 10118, 10136, 10158 and 10174, restated or extended that sunset; each is a later event with its own date. As last amended by Executive Order 10174 the adoption continues, for regulations under section 302 of the Act, “until January 31, 1951”, so the clause ends on January 31, 1951 (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins). Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10084 (14 FR 6245 (Federal Register of October 14, 1949)) concerns the order that adopts, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, the existing pay regulations, and fixes how long that adoption lasts. Executive Order 10084 was signed October 12, 1949 and takes effect October 1, 1949. Its sole paragraph adopts and prescribes the existing regulations under the Pay Readjustment Act of 1942, and existing departmental regulations and determinations, so far as applicable and appropriate, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Act, and its last sentence reads “This order shall take effect on October 1, 1949, and shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950”. Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap. The last held instrument is Executive Order 10174 (15 FR 7165 (Federal Register of October 26, 1950)), which continues the order, to the extent it adopts regulations under section 302 of the Act, “until January 31, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated at that last sunset, January 31, 1951, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The dossier's later-event chain and the held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 10084 (searched also with a trailing footnote digit) show no later instrument after Executive Order 10174: the Federal Register disposition-note search lists the five amendments named above, and the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. A later extension that the held corpus lacks is not excluded, which is the usual limit of a bounded search and is disclosed.

Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap. No instrument ends the parent order before January 31, 1951, and no end on a date between amendments is shown, because each amendment takes effect the day after the preceding date.","independent_command_check":"The clause has one function, which is to fix the duration of the adoption of regulations in Executive Order No. 10084, and has no separate command. The listed sections are separately sunsetted by the amendments, but the parent order as a whole ends when the last of them ends, which is the date recorded.","savings_check":"The order's text has no saving clause. Pay and allowances earned under the regulations while they were adopted are entitlements under the Career Compensation Act of 1949 and the regulations then in force; the held text creates no continuing duty after January 31, 1951, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring the adoption.","scope_check":"One operative paragraph (the adoption of regulations) whose closing sentence states the effective date and the original sunset; the dossier's single clause covers both."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order's text has no saving clause. Pay and allowances earned under the regulations while they were adopted are entitlements under the Career Compensation Act of 1949 and the regulations then in force; the held text creates no continuing duty after January 31, 1951, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring the adoption.

SUBPART— 1 9 4 9  FLAXSEED LOAN AND 
PURCHASE AGREEMENT PROGRAM
The regulations issued by the Com­
modity Credit Corporation with respect 
to the 1949 Flaxseed Loan and Purchase 
Agreement Program (14 F. R. 3728) are
amended by adding a paragraph at the 
end of paragraph (a), Loans, of §  643.133, 
Maturity and satisfaction,  so that the 
section reads as follows':
§  643.133 Maturity and satisfaction —
(a) Loans. Loans mature on demand 
but not later than January 31, 1950, for 
Arizona, California and Texas, and not 
later than April 30, 1950, for all other 
States. In the case of farm storage 
loans, the producer is required to pay 
off his loan on or before maturity, or to 
deliver the mortgaged flaxseed in ac­
cordance with instructions of the county 
committee. Credit will be given at the 
applicable loan value, according to grade 
and/or quality for the total quantity 
delivered, provided it was stored in the 
bin(s) in which the flaxseed under loan 
was stored. The loan value (county loan 
rates), for flaxseed delivered to CCC un­
der a farm storage loan will be set forth 
in this bulletin and in supplements or 
amendments thereto.
If the settlement value of the flaxseed 
delivered under a farm storage loan ex­
ceeds the amount due under the loan, 
the amount of the excess shall be paid 
to the producer by a sight draft drawn 
on CCC by the State PMA office.
If the settlement value of the flaxseed 
is less than the amount due on the loan, 
the amount of the deficiency, plus Inter­
est, shall be paid by the producer to 
CCC, or may be set off against any pay­
ment which would otherwise be made 
to the producer under any agricultural 
program administered by the Secretary 
of Agriculture, or any other payments 
which are due or may become due to the 
producer from CCC or any other agency 
of the United States. In the event the 
farm is sold or there is a change of ten­
ancy, the flaxseed may be delivered be­
fore the maturity date of the loan, upon 
prior approval by the county committee.
In the case of warehouse storage loans, 
if the producer does not repay his loan 
by maturity, CCC shall have the right 
to sell or pool the flaxseed in satisfaction 
of the loan In accordance with the pro­
visions of the note and loan agreement 
and §  643.134. Any payment due a pro­
ducer at the time of settlement on a 
warehouse storage loan, shall be made 
by the appropriate PMA commodity 
office.
Irrespective of the provisions of the 
mortgage supplement if farm-stored

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole paragraph provides that Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945 “is hereby revoked”. The order states no effective date, so the revocation took effect when signed on December 20, 1949. The filing stamp on the page reads December 22, 1949; that later filing date is disclosed as the alternative date if effectiveness is tied to filing, and the order itself does not say so. The command was exhausted by performance and the end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10093 (14 FR 7681 (Federal Register of December 23, 1949)) was signed December 20, 1949. The filing stamp printed after the order reads December 22, 1949, two days after signing. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence providing that Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945 “is hereby revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on December 20, 1949. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. The only other held text containing this order's number is the Federal Register page that reproduces this same order (EO_10092.txt, issue of December 23, 1949); it is the same instrument, not a later one. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945, which provided for coordination of the allocations of field positions subject to the Classification Act of 1923, as amended remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists, because the only command in the order is the revocation itself and it was performed when the order took effect on December 20, 1949. The order states no effective date other than signing. The filing stamp printed after the order reads December 22, 1949, two days after signing. If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. No later instrument is claimed as an end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The order creates no independent continuing duty, board, fund or authority that could outlast it; whatever the revoked instrument itself provided is outside this order and is not claimed here.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945, which provided for coordination of the allocations of field positions subject to the Classification Act of 1923, as amended stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945, which provided for coordination of the allocations of field positions subject to the Classification Act of 1923, as amended stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The clause restates the last paragraph of Executive Order No. 10084 so that the order ceases to be effective on March 31, 1950 instead of January 31, 1950. Under the owner ruling on restatements the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends. Executive Orders 10118, 10136, 10158 and 10174 restated or extended that sunset in turn, each recorded as a later event with its date; as last amended by Executive Order 10174 the parent continues, for section 302 regulations, “until January 31, 1951”, so the clause ends on January 31, 1951 (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins). Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10098 (15 FR 461 (Federal Register of January 27, 1950)) concerns the order that adopts, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, the existing pay regulations, and fixes how long that adoption lasts. Executive Order 10098 was signed January 25, 1950. Its only command amends the last paragraph of Executive Order No. 10084 to read that the order takes effect October 1, 1949 and ceases to be effective on March 31, 1950, replacing the January 31, 1950 sunset. Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap. The last held instrument is Executive Order 10174 (15 FR 7165 (Federal Register of October 26, 1950)), which continues the order, to the extent it adopts regulations under section 302 of the Act, “until January 31, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated at that last sunset, January 31, 1951, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The dossier's later-event chain and the held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 10084 (searched also with a trailing footnote digit) show no later instrument after Executive Order 10174: the Federal Register disposition-note search lists the five amendments named above, and the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. A later extension that the held corpus lacks is not excluded, which is the usual limit of a bounded search and is disclosed.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10107 (15 FR 701 (Federal Register of February 9, 1950)) was signed February 8, 1950. The filing stamp printed after the order reads February 8, 1950. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence ordering that Executive Order No. 8232 of September 5, 1939 “be, and it is hereby, revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on February 8, 1950. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 8232 of September 5, 1939, entitled “Control of the Panama Canal and the Canal Zone” remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists, because the only command in the order is the revocation itself and it was performed when the order took effect on February 8, 1950. The order states no effective date other than signing. The filing stamp printed after the order reads February 8, 1950. If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. No later instrument is claimed as an end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The order creates no independent continuing duty, board, fund or authority that could outlast it; whatever the revoked instrument itself provided is outside this order and is not claimed here.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 8232 of September 5, 1939, entitled “Control of the Panama Canal and the Canal Zone” stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence. The dossier's inventory ran the clause through an unrelated Department of Agriculture termination notice printed on the same Federal Register page; the inventory is corrected to the order's single sentence only."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The clause restates the last paragraph of Executive Order No. 10084 with a March 31, 1950 sunset and a proviso continuing regulations under five listed sections until June 30, 1950. Under the owner ruling on restatements the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends. Executive Orders 10136, 10158 and 10174 extended the listed sections in turn, each recorded as a later event with its date; as last amended by Executive Order 10174 the parent continues, for section 302 regulations, “until January 31, 1951”, so the clause ends on January 31, 1951 (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins). Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. research_rationale:
Executive Order 10118 (15 FR 1767 (Federal Register of March 30, 1950)) concerns the order that adopts, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, the existing pay regulations, and fixes how long that adoption lasts. Executive Order 10118 was signed March 27, 1950. Its only command restates the last paragraph of Executive Order No. 10084 (as amended by Executive Order No. 10098): the order ceases to be effective on March 31, 1950, except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Act, it continues until June 30, 1950. Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap. The last held instrument is Executive Order 10174 (15 FR 7165 (Federal Register of October 26, 1950)), which continues the order, to the extent it adopts regulations under section 302 of the Act, “until January 31, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated at that last sunset, January 31, 1951, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The dossier's later-event chain and the held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 10084 (searched also with a trailing footnote digit) show no later instrument after Executive Order 10174: the Federal Register disposition-note search lists the five amendments named above, and the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. A later extension that the held corpus lacks is not excluded, which is the usual limit of a bounded search and is disclosed.

Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap. No instrument ends the parent order before January 31, 1951, and no end on a date between amendments is shown, because each amendment takes effect the day after the preceding date.","independent_command_check":"The clause has one function, which is to fix the duration of the adoption of regulations in Executive Order No. 10084, and has no separate command. The listed sections are separately sunsetted by the amendments, but the parent order as a whole ends when the last of them ends, which is the date recorded.","savings_check":"The order's text has no saving clause. Pay and allowances earned under the regulations while they were adopted are entitlements under the Career Compensation Act of 1949 and the regulations then in force; the held text creates no continuing duty after January 31, 1951, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring the adoption.","scope_check":"One operative clause: the restatement of the last paragraph with its proviso."}

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10123
R evocation of E xecutive O rders N o. 
96351  of S eptember 29, 1945, and N o. 
99041  of N ovember 13, 1947
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
as President of the United States, it is 
ordered as follows:
Executive Order No. 9635 of September 
29, 1945, relating to the organization of
the Navy Department and the Naval 
Establishment, and Executive Order No. 
9904 of November 13,1947, amending the 
said Executive Order No. 9635, are hereby 
revoked.
The revocation made by this order 
shall not be construed as reviving Execu­
tive Order No, 8984 of December 18,1941, 
and Executive ¿Order No. 9096 of March
12, 1942 (as amended by Executive 
Order No. 9528 of March 2, 1945), re­
voked by the said Executive Order No. 
9635.
Harry S. T ruman
The W hite H ouse,
April 2d, 1950.
[P. R. Doc. 50-3445; Piled, Apr. 20, 1950;  
4:45 p. m.]
RULES AND REGULATIONS
TITLE 14— CIVIL AVIATION
Chapter II—-Civil Aeronautics Admin­
istration, Department of Commerce
Part 575—F ederal Civil Airports on 
Canton and W ake I slands
Under section 10 (a) of the Interna­
tional Aviation Facilities Act, the Ad­
ministrator of Civil ‘ Aeronautics is 
empowered and directed to do and per­
form all acts and things necessary or 
incident to the operation, protection, 
maintenance, improvement, and admin­
istration of airport property in territory 
outside the continental limits of the 
United States which he has acquired pur­
suant to the act or any other provision of 
law. This includes the power to make 
and amend such reasonable rules and 
regulations as he may deem necessary 
to the proper exercise of the powers 
granted by the section, and to make just 
and reasonable charges for aeronautical 
services, including but not limited to 
landing f66S.
Acting pursuant to the foregoing au­
thority, and in accordance with section 
3 (a) (3) of the Administrative Pro­
cedure Act, Part 575 is hereby adopted. 
The charges contained in this Part have 
been established at a level which is con­
sidered to be Within the ability of civil 
aviation to pay, and will be only partially 
compensatory at this time for the costs 
to the United States Government of 
maintaining and operating the landing 
areas involved. As ability of civil avia­
tion to pay changes, the level of charges 
will be revised with a view to recovering, 
as soon as practicable, the total costs of 
maintaining and operating the- landing 
areas.
SUBPABT A— INTRODUCTION
Sec. >
575.1 Explanation of terms.
SUBPART B— LANDING AND PARKING FEES
575.11 Landing fees.
575.12 Parking fees.
675.13 Alteration of fees.
575.14 Payment of fees.
SUBPART C— LOADING AND UNLOADING AREAS
575.21 Control of areas.
A u t h o r i t y: §§ 575.1 through 575.21 Issued  
under sec. 10, 62 Stat. 453; 49 U. S. C. Sup.,  
4159.
SUBPART A — INTRODUCTION
§  575.1 Explanation of terms —(a) 
Aircraft weight.  “Aircraft weight” shall 
mean the maximum take-off weight per­
mitted by the appropriate aeronautical 
authority of the State of manufacture
13 CFR, 1945 Supp.; i0 F. R. 12419.  
* •3  CFR, 1947 Supp.; 12 F. R. 7613.
of the aircraft. It shall be calculated to 
the nearest 1,000 pounds.
(b) Airport. “Airport” shall mean 
the Canton Island airport and the Wake 
Island airport operated by the Civil Aero­
nautics "  Administration.
(c) CAA. “CAA” shall mean the Civil 
Aeronautics Administration.
SUBPART B — LANDING AND PARKING FEES
§  575.11 Landing fees— t a) Rate of  
charge. A charge of 16 cents per 1,000 
pounds shall be made for each landing 
of an aircraft at the airport. (No addi­
tional charge .for each take-off shall be 
made.)(b) Exceptions to charge.  The follow­
ing aircraft shall not be subject to land­
ing fees:(1) Civil aircraft not engaged in com­
mercial operations;
(2) Aircraft engaged in test flights. 
(This shall not include survey and 
proving runs);
(3) Aircraft compelled to return after 
take-off;-
(4) Public aircraft not engaged in 
commercial operations.
§  575.12 Parking fees— (a) Hangar 
parking fee.  A charge of 5 cents per 
1,000 pounds of aircraft weight shall be 
made for each 6-hour period or fraction 
thereof during which an aircraft is 
parked in a hangar at the airport.
(b) Outside parking fee.  A charge of 
2.5 cents per 1,000 pounds of aircraft 
weight shall be made for each 6-hour 
period or fraction thereof during which 
an aircraft is parked outside at the air­
port. The charge shall start six hours 
after the plane lands.
§  575.13 Alteration of fees.  Charges 
for-aircraft based at the airport may be 
fixed by the CAA Regional Administrator 
having jurisdiction over the airport, 
without regard to the landing and park­
ing fees provided in §§ 575.11 and 575.12.
§  575.14 Payment of fees —(a) Time 
and means of payment.  Fees shall be 
paid in United States dollars at the time 
use is made of the airport.
(b) Exceptions to time of payment.  
Scheduled air carriers and other aircraft 
operators may make prior financial ar­
rangements with the CAA official in 
charge of the airport. These arrange­
ments may include provision for pay­
ment on a monthly or other suitable 
basis.
SUBPART C — LOADING AND UNLOADING A REAS
§  575.21 Control of areas.  The CAA 
official in charge of the airport shall have 
full control of the loading and unloading 
areas to insure efficient and noh-discrim-
inatory utilization. Such authority shall 
inplude, but shall not necessarily be lim­
ited to, the right to:
(a) Assign space and sequence of use 
when lie-concludes that it is necessary 
or advisable;
(b) Order the movement of a stand­
ing aircraft to conform with assign­
ments under paragraph (a) of this 
sêction ;
(c) Assess an excess parking fee of 
$5 per hour for non-conformity with 
paragraph (b) of this section.
This part shall become effective May 1, 
1950.
[seal] D onald W. N yrop,
Acting Administrator of  
Civil Aeronautics.

8:46 a. m.]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The first sentence provides that Executive Order No. 9635 and Executive Order No. 9904 “are hereby revoked”. The order states no effective date, so the revocation took effect when signed on April 20, 1950 (the filing stamp reads April 20, 1950 as well). The command was exhausted by performance on that date and the end source is the order's own text.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The second sentence says the revocation made by this order shall not be construed as reviving Executive Order No. 8984 and Executive Order No. 9096 (as amended), which Executive Order No. 9635 had revoked. It limits only the effect of the revocation performed in the first sentence, so it operated once, when that revocation took effect on April 20, 1950, and has no separate continuing command. Its consequence, that the two named earlier orders were not revived, is disclosed as a surviving effect and is not claimed as an operative command.
